summary: TS SDK streaming session: mid-stream token refresh splits multipart funcall payloads and causes duplicate external tool invocations
description:
Issue summary:
The customer reports duplicate external tool/webhook executions when using the TypeScript SDK streaming endpoint with function/tool calling enabled. The duplicates manifest only when an auth token refresh occurs while a single multipart funcall response is being streamed (large payload split across SSE frames).

Impact:
- Several webhook recipients received duplicate job runs (idempotency tokens not de-duplicating).
- Customer reported intermittent double-charges for downstream processing and increased error rate in their system (customer-visible).
- Affects a production Dedicated account in us-east.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- SDK: typescript v1.8.2 (@redwood/sdk), using SSE streaming to receive multipart function call responses
- Deployment: prod (us-east-1), model redwood/gptk-13b-quant pinned
- Network: behind customer edge proxy (nginx) + internal API gateway

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Create a streaming generation that triggers a function call which returns a large base64 payload (~120KB) split across multiple SSE messages.
2. Start streaming via TS SDK client with connection long-lived (~90s).
3. During the stream, the auth token is refreshed by the customer's auth middleware (rotates API key header mid-connection).
4. The client receives the latter part of the multipart funcall as a separate SSE frame; server-side logs show the funcall completion event arriving twice to the webhook handler.

Expected behavior:
- A single funcall completion webhook should be emitted and accepted, with idempotency safeguards preventing re-execution. Multipart streaming should reassemble the complete payload reliably regardless of token refresh.

Actual behavior:
- Two distinct webhook invocations observed: one with a truncated idempotency header (token-derived nonce shortened) and a second with the complete header. Both were treated as independent by the customer's webhook endpoint and resulted in duplicated downstream work.

Logs / Evidence provided by customer:
- SSE trace (timestamps): client received frames at 12:03:01, 12:03:14, token refresh at 12:03:10.
- Webhook logs show two POSTs: 12:03:15 and 12:03:16 with different X-Idempotency headers (one truncated).
- Customer attached a HAR of the streaming connection and the webhook payloads.

Customer's workaround attempts:
- They implemented a server-side dedupe using request body hash but saw increased latency and occasional misses because the truncated header variant had slightly different body chunk boundaries.

Additional notes from customer:
- Works reliably when they disable token auto-rotation (long-lived key) or when payloads are small and do not cross frame boundaries.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Support (Asha Patel): Ticket created after initial report from customer. Collected HAR and webhook logs. Escalated due to potential for duplicate downstream charges.

2026-03-12 - Engineer (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged; initial hypothesis: header rewriting/normalization by customer proxy or our gateway during mid-stream auth header rotation could be mangling idempotency tokens. Will reproduce locally by simulating token rotation.

2026-03-12 - Customer (NimbleDocs - eng lead Maria Chen): We can reproduce consistently when using our internal auth middleware that swaps Authorization header mid-connection. Providing access to a staging tenant for deeper traces.

2026-03-13 - Support (Asha Patel): Added links to customer's staging access and uploaded HAR to internal case storage. Requested a scoped test script from Eng to validate dedupe across rotation events.

2026-03-13 - Engineer (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally using TS SDK v1.8.2 with an auth rotation simulation. Observed SSE frame boundary arrives as separate server events when header changes; idempotency header got truncated by chunking at the proxy layer in test setup. Filing follow-up with gateway and SDK teams.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Token rotation mid-stream leads to two independent request contexts at the gateway, each with different idempotency header values. 2) Edge proxy (nginx) or customer middleware rewrites/splits headers when a connection-level header mutation occurs. 3) SDK may re-emit finalization frames after re-auth handshake. Actions taken: reproduced with local proxy, captured tcpdump and SSE frames, confirmed header truncation occurs before our webhook delivery. Correlated trace ids: trace-redwood-6132. Checked gateway codepath handling streaming auth; identified a code-path where partial frames are buffered and re-emitted on auth-change event. Raised a PR proposal to ensure atomic delivery of funcall completion and to drop incomplete idempotency headers at the gateway if re-auth occurs mid-stream. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1297
resolution: Workaround provided: customer disabled automatic auth rotation for critical streams while we release a fix. Engineering change: implemented gateway guard to preserve full idempotency headers or to reject mid-stream header mutations (reject-with-419) so clients must re-establish. Patch deployed to staging 2026-03-13; verified in customer's staging tenant. Rollout plan: Canary to 10% of prod traffic on 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-17 pending monitoring. Customer follow-up: NimbleDocs will re-enable rotation in staging and confirm dedupe. Follow-ups: SDK team to add documentation and warnings about mid-stream header rotation and recommend using the SDK token-refresh hooks to refresh before starting long-lived streams.
postmortem_followup_tasks: Add SDK guidance: explicit token-refresh-before-stream checklist (SDK-TS docs)
Improve gateway: atomicize streaming frame emission on header changes (infra PR #1297)
Add a streaming integration test that simulates token rotation and validates idempotency header integrity
Customer success: schedule a walkthrough with NimbleDocs to validate rollout
